newsitem.title: USA: AMEX no comment on Apple options review.
newsitem.headline: AMEX no comment on Apple options review.

text.p: The American Stock Exchange (AMEX) had no comment Wednesday on a possible investigation into trading of Apple Computer Inc options.
"Anytime there is volume that's out of the ordinary we will look into it," an exchange spokeswoman said. "But there is a distinction betwween an investigation and looking into something."
Regarding any Apple investigation, she said: "We can't comment."
Volume in Apple call options had picked up sharply in the last several sessions as the stock moved higher on news reports co-founder Steve Jobs may return as chief executive.
But on Wednesday, Apple said Microsoft Corp would invest $150 million in Apple stock.

The Cupertino, Calif.-based company also named Jobs, who is currently a strategic advisor to the company, Oracle Corp Chairman Larry Ellison, former International Business Machines Corp Chief Financial Officer Jerome York and Inuit Inc Chief Excecutive Bill Campbell to its board of directors.
Three current board members, A.C. "Mike" Markkula, a one-time chairman and early Apple investor, Katherine Hudson and Bernard Goldstein, resigned.
The news drove Apple shares up 6-9/16 to 26-5/16 on heavy volume of more than 37 million shares.

Lawrence McMillan, head of McMillan Analysis Corp and publisher of the Daily Volume Alert, said the recent increase in Apple options volume appeared at the time to be from investors responding to the news reports.
"In retrospect, I guess probably somebody knew that they were working on a deal," he said. "That would be my analysis after the fact."
According to data from McMillan, Apple options volume Monday rose to 12,424 contracts from an average of 3,050. Of that, 10,629 was call volume.
On Wednesday, more than 61,000 Apple options traded.
The Amex spokeswoman said that for all the month of July approximately 97,000 options traded.
